records.source: וַיְהִ֗י אַחַר֙ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה כֶּ֧רֶם הָיָ֛ה לְנָב֥וֹת הַיִּזְרְעֵאלִ֖י אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּיִזְרְעֶ֑אל אֵ֚צֶל הֵיכַ֣ל אַחְאָ֔ב מֶ֖לֶךְ שֹׁמְרֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: And it was after the things the these: a vineyard was to Naboth the Jezreelite, which [was] in Jezreel, beside [the] palace of Ahab king of Samaria.
pieces: Some time after these events, Naboth the Jezreelite owned a vineyard in Jezreel, beside the palace of Ahab, the king of Samaria.

L.1: And it happened after these things: Naboth the Jezreelite had a vineyard that [was] in Jezreel, beside the palace of Ahab king of Samaria.

R.1: Some time later, a man named Naboth from Jezreel owned a vineyard in the town of Jezreel. It was next to the palace of King Ahab, who ruled from Samaria.

decisions.choice: Jezreel: a town where Ahab kept a second royal palace; Samaria was his capital
decisions.reason: Jezreel stood on the edge of the fertile Jezreel Valley, and Ahab had a residence there as well as in Samaria (18:45-46). His father Omri had built Samaria as the capital (16:24, 29), so Ahab is called "king of Samaria", the city he ruled from.

decisions.choice: after these things: after the wars with Aram in chapter 20, in the Hebrew order of the chapters
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew text this story follows the Aramean wars of chapter 20. The ancient Greek translation places it straight after chapter 19, so that the stories of Elijah run together and the two accounts of Ahab's wars with Aram (chapters 20 and 22) stand side by side. The Hebrew order is followed. The connection is loose: "after these things" only says that the events came later.

decisions.choice: King Ahab, who ruled from Samaria
decisions.reason: Readable explains the title "king of Samaria" (m1), so that the reader does not think Ahab ruled only one city.

records.heading: Naboth's vineyard

records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אַחְאָ֣ב אֶל־נָב֣וֹת׀לֵאמֹר֩׀תְּנָה־לִּ֨י אֶֽת־כַּרְמְךָ֜ וִֽיהִי־לִ֣י לְגַן־יָרָ֗ק כִּ֣י ה֤וּא קָרוֹב֙ אֵ֣צֶל בֵּיתִ֔י וְאֶתְּנָ֤ה לְךָ֙ תַּחְתָּ֔יו כֶּ֖רֶם ט֣וֹב מִמֶּ֑נּוּ אִ֚ם ט֣וֹב בְּעֵינֶ֔יךָ אֶתְּנָה־לְךָ֥ כֶ֖סֶף מְחִ֥יר זֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And spoke Ahab to Naboth, saying, Give to me your vineyard, and let it be to me for a garden of vegetables, because it [is] near, beside my house; and I will give to you in its place a vineyard better than it; if [it is] good in your eyes, I will give to you silver, [the] price of this.
pieces: Ahab said to Naboth, "Let me have your vineyard to use as a vegetable garden, since it is close to my palace. In its place I will give you a better vineyard, or, if you prefer, I will pay you its value in silver."

L.2: And Ahab spoke to Naboth, saying, "Give me your vineyard, so that it may be mine for a vegetable garden, because it [is] near, beside my house; and I will give you in its place a vineyard better than it. If [it is] good in your eyes, I will give you silver, the price of it."

R.2: Ahab said to Naboth, "Give me your vineyard. It is close to my palace, and I want to make it into a vegetable garden. I will give you a better vineyard for it. Or if you would rather have money, I will pay you what it is worth."

decisions.choice: my house: the king's palace
decisions.reason: "House" here is the palace of verse 1, which stood next to the vineyard.

decisions.choice: a vegetable garden: a garden of greens and herbs for the palace
decisions.reason: Ahab wants to turn a vineyard, which takes years to grow, into a kitchen garden. The same phrase describes the watered garden plots of Egypt (Deuteronomy 11:10).

decisions.choice: if it is good in your eyes: if you prefer
decisions.reason: The offer is fair on its face: a better vineyard or the full price. What Ahab does not see is that the land is not Naboth's to trade (verse 3).

decisions.choice: palace
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "palace" for "house" (m1); Literal keeps "house".

decisions.choice: money
decisions.reason: Silver was weighed out as payment; Literal and Balanced keep "silver", and Readable says "money", which is what it was used as.

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר נָב֖וֹת אֶל־אַחְאָ֑ב חָלִ֤ילָה לִּי֙ מֵֽיהוָ֔ה מִתִּתִּ֛י אֶת־נַחֲלַ֥ת אֲבֹתַ֖י לָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And said Naboth to Ahab, Far be it to me from Yahweh, from my giving the inheritance of my fathers to you.
pieces: But Naboth said to Ahab, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} forbid that I hand over to you the inheritance of my ancestors!"

L.3: And Naboth said to Ahab, "Far be it from me, by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, that I should give the inheritance of my fathers to you."

R.3: But Naboth answered Ahab, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} keep me from ever doing that! This land has come down to me from my ancestors. I will not give it to you."

decisions.choice: far be it from me by Yahweh: a refusal under oath, as something Yahweh himself would forbid
decisions.reason: The phrase calls the act unthinkable, even profane, and naming Yahweh makes it an oath (compare 1 Samuel 24:7; 26:11). Naboth refuses as a matter of faithfulness to God, not of taste or price.

decisions.choice: the inheritance of my fathers: family land given to the tribes, which was not to pass out of the family for good
decisions.reason: Each family's land came to it from the division of the land under Joshua, and the law kept it in the family: "the land must not be sold permanently, for the land is mine" (Leviticus 25:23), and "each of the Israelites shall hold on to the inheritance of the tribe of his fathers" (Numbers 36:7). Land sold in hard times went back to the family (Leviticus 25:25-28). For Naboth to sell or trade it to the crown would be to give up what Yahweh had given his family.

decisions.choice: ancestors
decisions.reason: "Fathers" means forefathers; Balanced and Readable say "ancestors", as in the regnal formulas of Kings.

decisions.choice: This land has come down to me from my ancestors. I will not give it to you.
decisions.reason: Readable explains "inheritance" (m2) and splits the oath from the refusal.

records.source: וַיָּבֹא֩ אַחְאָ֨ב אֶל־בֵּית֜וֹ סַ֣ר וְזָעֵ֗ף עַל־הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֣ר אֵלָ֗יו נָבוֹת֙ הַיִּזְרְעֵאלִ֔י וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לֹֽא־אֶתֵּ֥ן לְךָ֖ אֶת־נַחֲלַ֣ת אֲבוֹתָ֑י וַיִּשְׁכַּב֙ עַל־מִטָּת֔וֹ וַיַּסֵּ֥ב אֶת־פָּנָ֖יו וְלֹֽא־אָ֥כַל לָֽחֶם׃
records.gloss: And came Ahab to his house sullen and angry because of the word which spoke to him Naboth the Jezreelite, and he said, Not I will give to you the inheritance of my fathers; and he lay on his bed and turned his face and not he ate food.
pieces: So Ahab went home sullen and angry because of what Naboth the Jezreelite had said to him: "I will not give you the inheritance of my ancestors." He lay down on his bed, turned his face away, and would not eat.

L.4: And Ahab came to his house sullen and vexed because of the word that Naboth the Jezreelite had spoken to him, when he said, "I will not give you the inheritance of my fathers." And he lay down on his bed and turned away his face and did not eat food.

R.4: So Ahab went home upset and angry because Naboth from Jezreel had told him, "I will not give you the land I received from my ancestors." He lay on his bed, turned his face away, and refused to eat.

decisions.choice: sullen and vexed: the same mood as in 20:43
decisions.reason: The same two words describe Ahab going home after the prophet condemned him for letting Ben-hadad go (20:43). The writer shows the king sulking a second time when he does not get his way.

decisions.choice: lay on his bed, turned his face, did not eat: a show of sulking
decisions.reason: The king takes to his bed and refuses food, like a child who has been told no. Jezebel at once sees that something is wrong (verse 5).

decisions.choice: he said: Naboth's words as Ahab remembers them
decisions.reason: Ahab repeats Naboth's refusal but leaves out the oath by Yahweh that Naboth gave as his reason (verse 3).

decisions.choice: upset
decisions.reason: Readable uses an everyday word for "sullen" (resentful and withdrawn).

records.source: וַתָּבֹ֥א אֵלָ֖יו אִיזֶ֣בֶל אִשְׁתּ֑וֹ וַתְּדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלָ֗יו מַה־זֶּה֙ רוּחֲךָ֣ סָרָ֔ה וְאֵינְךָ֖ אֹכֵ֥ל לָֽחֶם׃
records.gloss: And came to him Jezebel his wife and spoke to him, Why [is] this, your spirit sullen, and not you [are] eating food?
pieces: His wife Jezebel came in and asked him, "Why are you so downcast that you will not eat?"

L.5: And Jezebel his wife came to him and said to him, "Why [is] this, [that] your spirit [is] sullen and you are not eating food?"

R.5: His wife Jezebel came to him and asked, "Why are you so upset? Why will you not eat anything?"

decisions.choice: Jezebel: the Phoenician queen, daughter of the king of the Sidonians
decisions.reason: Ahab married Jezebel daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians and served Baal (16:31). She had killed the prophets of Yahweh (18:4) and sworn to kill Elijah (19:2).

decisions.choice: your spirit sullen: your mood low and resentful
decisions.reason: "Spirit" here means mood or temper; "sullen" is the word used of Ahab in verse 4.

decisions.choice: downcast
decisions.reason: Balanced describes the mood in one word; Literal keeps "spirit" and "sullen".

records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלֶ֗יהָ כִּֽי־אֲ֠דַבֵּר אֶל־נָב֨וֹת הַיִּזְרְעֵאלִ֜י וָאֹ֣מַר ל֗וֹ תְּנָה־לִּ֤י אֶֽת־כַּרְמְךָ֙ בְּכֶ֔סֶף א֚וֹ אִם־חָפֵ֣ץ אַתָּ֔ה אֶתְּנָה־לְךָ֥ כֶ֖רֶם תַּחְתָּ֑יו וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לֹֽא־אֶתֵּ֥ן לְךָ֖ אֶת־כַּרְמִֽי׃
records.gloss: And he spoke to her, Because I spoke to Naboth the Jezreelite and said to him, Give to me your vineyard for silver, or if desiring you [are], I will give to you a vineyard in its place; and he said, Not I will give to you my vineyard.
pieces: He told her, "I spoke to Naboth the Jezreelite and said to him, 'Sell me your vineyard, or if you prefer, I will give you another vineyard in its place.' But he said, 'I will not give you my vineyard.'"

L.6: And he said to her, "Because I spoke to Naboth the Jezreelite and said to him, 'Give me your vineyard for silver, or, if you desire [it], I will give you a vineyard in its place'; and he said, 'I will not give you my vineyard.'"

R.6: He answered, "I talked to Naboth from Jezreel. I said, 'Sell me your vineyard. Or if you would rather, I will give you another vineyard in place of it.' But he said, 'I will not give you my vineyard.'"

decisions.choice: my vineyard: Ahab's retelling leaves out Naboth's reason
decisions.reason: Ahab reports the refusal as "I will not give you my vineyard". He drops the oath by Yahweh and the words "the inheritance of my fathers" (verse 3), so Naboth sounds merely stubborn. He also names the money first and the exchange second, the reverse of verse 2.

decisions.choice: Sell me your vineyard
decisions.reason: "Give me ... for silver" means a sale, so Balanced and Readable say "sell"; Literal keeps the wording.

records.source: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ אִיזֶ֣בֶל אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ אַתָּ֕ה עַתָּ֛ה תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה מְלוּכָ֖ה עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל ק֤וּם אֱכָל־לֶ֨חֶם֙ וְיִטַ֣ב לִבֶּ֔ךָ אֲנִי֙ אֶתֵּ֣ן לְךָ֔ אֶת־כֶּ֖רֶם נָב֥וֹת הַיִּזְרְעֵאלִֽי׃
records.gloss: And said to him Jezebel his wife, You now exercise kingship over Israel? Arise, eat food, and let be good your heart; I will give to you the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite.
pieces: His wife Jezebel said to him, "Are you not the one who rules as king over Israel now? Get up and eat something, and cheer up. I myself will get you the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite."

L.7: And Jezebel his wife said to him, "[Is it] you [who] now exercise kingship over Israel? Get up, eat food, and let your heart be glad. I will give you the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite."

R.7: His wife Jezebel said, "You are the king of Israel, are you not? Get up and eat something. Cheer up! I will get Naboth's vineyard for you myself."

decisions.choice: you now exercise kingship over Israel?: a scornful question, a challenge to act like a king
alternatives: an exclamation: you are the king now, so act like it
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no question word; the emphatic "you" and the tone show Jezebel mocking Ahab's helplessness. It can also be read as an exclamation ("You are the one who rules Israel now!"), with the same point: a king should take what he wants.

decisions.choice: kingship: Jezebel's idea of royal power, against Israel's law for kings
decisions.reason: In Israel the king was under the law (Deuteronomy 17:18-20), and Samuel had warned that a king would "take your fields and your vineyards" (1 Samuel 8:14). Jezebel, raised in a Phoenician court, treats the king's wish as enough reason to take a subject's land.

decisions.choice: I will give you: Jezebel takes the matter on herself
decisions.reason: The pronoun "I" is written out for emphasis: what Ahab could not get, she will.

decisions.choice: cheer up
decisions.reason: "Let your heart be good" means to be glad again; Literal keeps the picture.

decisions.choice: Are you not the one who rules ...? (Balanced); You are the king of Israel, are you not? (Readable)
decisions.reason: Both levels make the scornful question plain in English (m1).

records.source: וַתִּכְתֹּ֤ב סְפָרִים֙ בְּשֵׁ֣ם אַחְאָ֔ב וַתַּחְתֹּ֖ם בְּחֹתָמ֑וֹ וַתִּשְׁלַ֣ח סְפָרִ֗ים אֶל־הַזְקֵנִ֤יםוְאֶל־הַֽחֹרִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּעִיר֔וֹ הַיֹּשְׁבִ֖ים אֶת־נָבֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And she wrote letters in [the] name of Ahab and sealed with his seal, and she sent the letters to the elders and to the nobles who [were] in his city, the [ones] dwelling with Naboth.
pieces: So she wrote letters in Ahab's name and put his seal on them, and she sent them to the leading men and elders of Naboth's city, who lived there with him.

L.8: And she wrote letters in Ahab's name and sealed [them] with his seal, and she sent the letters to the elders and to the nobles who [were] in his city, who lived with Naboth.

R.8: So Jezebel wrote some letters as if they came from Ahab, and she stamped them with his royal seal. She sent them to the elders and other leaders in Naboth's town, who were his neighbors.

decisions.choice: sealed with his seal: marked with the king's stamp, giving the letters his authority
decisions.reason: A seal was a stamp or ring pressed into clay or wax to show who sent a document (Esther 8:8). Letters under the king's seal carried the king's command.

decisions.choice: nobles: the free-born leading men of the town
decisions.reason: The word names the leading citizens who, with the elders, governed a town (Nehemiah 2:16).

decisions.choice: his city: Naboth's city, Jezreel
decisions.reason: "His" refers to Naboth, as the next words show: the elders who lived with him, that is, his fellow townsmen.

decisions.choice: letters: the form read aloud
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) have "the letters"; the form marked to be read aloud (qere) has "letters". The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: as if they came from Ahab
decisions.reason: "In Ahab's name" means she wrote as though Ahab had sent them; Readable says so.

records.source: וַתִּכְתֹּ֥ב בַּסְּפָרִ֖ים לֵאמֹ֑ר קִֽרְאוּ־צ֔וֹם וְהוֹשִׁ֥יבוּ אֶת־נָב֖וֹת בְּרֹ֥אשׁ הָעָֽם׃
records.gloss: And she wrote in the letters, saying, Proclaim a fast, and seat Naboth at [the] head of the people.
pieces: In the letters she wrote: "Proclaim a fast, and seat Naboth at the front of the people.

L.9: And she wrote in the letters, saying, "Proclaim a fast, and seat Naboth at the head of the people.

R.9: This is what she wrote in the letters: "Call the people together for a day of fasting. Seat Naboth in front, where everyone can see him.

decisions.choice: proclaim a fast: call the town to a public day of fasting
decisions.reason: A public fast was called when a community faced disaster or feared that some sin had brought God's anger on it (Judges 20:26; 1 Samuel 7:6; Joel 1:14). It suggested that a guilty person had to be found, as Achan was (Joshua 7).

decisions.choice: at the head of the people: in front of the assembly, in full view
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean a seat of honor (1 Samuel 9:22) or simply the most prominent place, where Naboth would be seen by all when the charge was made. Either way his fall would be public.

decisions.choice: the letter begins: its words run through verse 10
decisions.reason: The quotation opens here and closes at the end of verse 10.

records.source: וְ֠הוֹשִׁיבוּ שְׁנַ֨יִם אֲנָשִׁ֥ים בְּנֵֽי־בְלִיַּעַל֮ נֶגְדּוֹ֒ וִיעִדֻ֣הוּ לֵאמֹ֔ר בֵּרַ֥כְתָּ אֱלֹהִ֖ים וָמֶ֑לֶךְ וְהוֹצִיאֻ֥הוּ וְסִקְלֻ֖הוּ וְיָמֹֽת׃
records.gloss: And seat two men, sons of worthlessness, opposite him, and let them testify against him, saying, You blessed God and [the] king; and bring him out and stone him, and let him die.
pieces: Seat two worthless men opposite him, and have them bring this charge against him: 'You have cursed God and the king.' Then take him outside and stone him until he dies."

L.10: And seat two men, sons of worthlessness, opposite him, and let them testify against him, saying, 'You have cursed God and the king.' Then bring him out and stone him, so that he dies."

R.10: Put two worthless men across from him, and have them accuse him. Have them say, 'You cursed God and the king!' Then take him out and kill him by throwing stones at him."

decisions.choice: sons of worthlessness: worthless men, scoundrels
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 20:1 and 1 Samuel 2:12, the word means worthlessness or wickedness. Here they are men ready to lie under oath against an innocent neighbor.

decisions.choice: cursed: the Hebrew says "blessed", written in place of "cursed"
decisions.reason: To avoid writing the words "curse God", the Hebrew uses "bless" where the sense is plainly "curse", as in Job 1:5, 11; 2:5, 9 and again in verse 13. A charge of blessing God would be no crime; the sense is "cursed".

decisions.choice: two witnesses, cursing God and the king, stoning: the law's own forms used for murder
decisions.reason: The law forbade cursing God or a ruler (Exodus 22:27); one who cursed God was to be stoned (Leviticus 24:15-16). A death sentence needed two witnesses (Numbers 35:30; Deuteronomy 17:6; 19:15). Jezebel follows every form of the law to kill an innocent man.

decisions.choice: cursed
decisions.reason: Every level, Literal included, gives the sense "cursed" (m2), since "blessed" would say the opposite of what is meant; the decision keeps the word written.

decisions.choice: kill him by throwing stones at him
decisions.reason: Readable says what stoning was.

records.source: וַיַּעֲשׂוּ֩ אַנְשֵׁ֨י עִיר֜וֹ הַזְּקֵנִ֣ים וְהַחֹרִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר הַיֹּֽשְׁבִים֙ בְּעִיר֔וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר שָׁלְחָ֥ה אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם אִיזָ֑בֶל כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר כָּתוּב֙ בַּסְּפָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁלְחָ֖ה אֲלֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And did [the] men of his city, the elders and the nobles who [were] the [ones] dwelling in his city, according to what sent to them Jezebel, just as [it was] written in the letters which she sent to them.
pieces: The men of Naboth's city, the elders and leading men who lived there, did as Jezebel had instructed them, exactly as it was written in the letters she had sent them.

L.11: And the men of his city, the elders and the nobles who lived in his city, did as Jezebel had sent [word] to them, just as [it was] written in the letters that she had sent to them.

R.11: The elders and leaders of Naboth's town did exactly what Jezebel told them to do in her letters.

decisions.choice: according to what Jezebel sent, just as it was written: exact obedience
decisions.reason: The repeated phrases stress that the town leaders carried out the plan to the letter; no one refused. They also name Jezebel, not Ahab, as the sender: they knew whose letters these were.

decisions.choice: one shorter sentence
decisions.reason: Readable gives the repeated phrases once, keeping the point that they did exactly what Jezebel wrote.

records.source: קָרְא֖וּ צ֑וֹם וְהֹשִׁ֥יבוּ אֶת־נָב֖וֹת בְּרֹ֥אשׁ הָעָֽם׃
records.gloss: They proclaimed a fast and seated Naboth at [the] head of the people.
pieces: They proclaimed a fast and seated Naboth at the front of the people.

L.12: They proclaimed a fast and seated Naboth at the head of the people.

R.12: They called the people together for a day of fasting and seated Naboth in front, where everyone could see him.

decisions.choice: they proclaimed: the orders of verse 9 carried out word for word
decisions.reason: The verse repeats Jezebel's words from verse 9 as a plain report, without even "and" to begin it.

records.gloss: And came the two men, sons of worthlessness, and sat opposite him; and testified against him the men of worthlessness, against Naboth, before the people, saying, Blessed Naboth God and [the] king; and they brought him out outside of the city and stoned him with stones, and he died.
pieces: Then the two worthless men came in and sat opposite him, and the worthless men brought their charge against Naboth in front of the people: "Naboth has cursed God and the king." So they led him out of the city and stoned him until he died.

L.13: And the two men, sons of worthlessness, came in and sat opposite him; and the men of worthlessness testified against him, against Naboth, before the people, saying, "Naboth has cursed God and the king." And they brought him out outside the city and stoned him with stones, and he died.

R.13: Then the two worthless men came and sat across from Naboth. In front of all the people they accused him. "Naboth cursed God and the king!" they said. So they took Naboth outside the town and threw stones at him until he died.

decisions.choice: cursed: "blessed" written in place of "cursed"
decisions.reason: As in verse 10.

decisions.choice: outside the city: where the law placed executions
decisions.reason: A person sentenced to stoning was taken outside the camp or town (Leviticus 24:14; Numbers 15:35-36; Deuteronomy 17:5).

decisions.choice: he died: and, by 2 Kings 9:26, his sons with him
decisions.reason: Later Jehu recalls "the blood of Naboth and the blood of his sons" (2 Kings 9:26). With his heirs dead, there was no one left in the family to claim the land, and it could pass to the crown.

decisions.choice: threw stones at him until he died
decisions.reason: Readable says what stoning was, as in verse 10.

records.source: וַֽיִּשְׁלְח֖וּ אֶל־אִיזֶ֣בֶל לֵאמֹ֑ר סֻקַּ֥ל נָב֖וֹת וַיָּמֹֽת׃
records.gloss: And they sent to Jezebel, saying, Was stoned Naboth and he died.
pieces: Then they sent a message to Jezebel: "Naboth has been stoned, and he is dead."

L.14: And they sent to Jezebel, saying, "Naboth has been stoned and is dead."

R.14: They sent this message to Jezebel: "Naboth has been stoned. He is dead."

decisions.choice: to Jezebel: the report goes to the one who gave the orders
decisions.reason: The letters went out in Ahab's name, but the elders report to Jezebel. They knew who was behind the plan.

records.source: וַֽיְהִי֙ כִּשְׁמֹ֣עַ אִיזֶ֔בֶל כִּֽי־סֻקַּ֥ל נָב֖וֹת וַיָּמֹ֑ת וַתֹּ֨אמֶר אִיזֶ֜בֶל אֶל־אַחְאָ֗ב ק֣וּם רֵ֞שׁ אֶת־כֶּ֣רֶם׀נָב֣וֹת הַיִּזְרְעֵאלִ֗י אֲשֶׁ֤ר מֵאֵן֙ לָתֶת־לְךָ֣ בְכֶ֔סֶף כִּ֣י אֵ֥ין נָב֛וֹת חַ֖י כִּי־מֵֽת׃
records.gloss: And it was, as heard Jezebel that was stoned Naboth and he died, and said Jezebel to Ahab, Arise, take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, which he refused to give to you for silver; for not is Naboth alive, but dead.
pieces: As soon as Jezebel heard that Naboth had been stoned and was dead, she told Ahab, "Get up and take possession of the vineyard that Naboth the Jezreelite refused to sell you. Naboth is no longer alive. He is dead."

L.15: And it happened, when Jezebel heard that Naboth had been stoned and was dead, Jezebel said to Ahab, "Get up, take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, which he refused to give you for silver; for Naboth is not alive, but dead."

R.15: When Jezebel heard that Naboth had been stoned and killed, she told Ahab, "Get up! Go and take over Naboth's vineyard, the one he would not sell you. Naboth is not alive anymore. He is dead."

decisions.choice: take possession: the word used of taking the promised land
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for Israel taking possession of the land from the nations (Deuteronomy 1:8; Joshua 1:11). Ahab is to take over an Israelite's inheritance as if it were conquered land. The word returns in verses 16, 18 and 19.

decisions.choice: not alive, but dead: Jezebel says only that he is dead, not how
decisions.reason: She tells Ahab nothing of the trial or the false witnesses, and Ahab asks nothing.

decisions.choice: refused to sell you
decisions.reason: "Refused to give you for silver" means he would not sell; Literal keeps the wording.

records.source: וַיְהִ֛י כִּשְׁמֹ֥עַ אַחְאָ֖ב כִּ֣י מֵ֣ת נָב֑וֹת וַיָּ֣קָם אַחְאָ֗ב לָרֶ֛דֶת אֶל־כֶּ֛רֶם נָב֥וֹת הַיִּזְרְעֵאלִ֖י לְרִשְׁתּֽוֹ׃ס
records.gloss: And it was, as heard Ahab that dead [was] Naboth, and arose Ahab to go down to [the] vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, to take possession of it.
pieces: Once Ahab heard that Naboth was dead, he rose and went down to Naboth the Jezreelite's vineyard to take possession of it.

L.16: And it happened, when Ahab heard that Naboth was dead, Ahab got up to go down to the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, to take possession of it.

R.16: When Ahab heard about Naboth's death, he got up and went down to Naboth's vineyard to take it for himself.

decisions.choice: go down: from the hill city of Samaria down to Jezreel
decisions.reason: Samaria stood on a hill (16:24); Jezreel lay lower, at the edge of its valley. Verse 18 also says Ahab "has gone down" to the vineyard.

decisions.choice: Ahab got up to go down: the Hebrew text has no word of mourning here
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation adds that Ahab tore his clothes and put on sackcloth when he heard of Naboth's death, before going down to the vineyard. The Hebrew text, which is followed, has nothing of the kind until Ahab hears Elijah's words (verse 27).

decisions.choice: take it for himself
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of "take possession of" (verse 15) in plain words.

records.gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,
pieces: Then the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Elijah the Tishbite:

L.17: And the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,

R.17: Then this message from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Elijah from Tishbe:

decisions.choice: the Tishbite: from Tishbe in Gilead
decisions.reason: Elijah was introduced as "the Tishbite, from the settlers of Gilead" (17:1). He has not appeared since his call of Elisha (19:19-21).

decisions.choice: the word of Yahweh came: God acts where the town's leaders did not
decisions.reason: The elders and nobles of Jezreel went along with the crime. Yahweh, who saw it, sends his prophet to the king.

decisions.choice: Elijah from Tishbe
decisions.reason: Readable says where "the Tishbite" comes from.

records.heading: Elijah confronts Ahab

records.source: ק֣וּם רֵ֗ד לִקְרַ֛את אַחְאָ֥ב מֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּשֹׁמְר֑וֹן הִנֵּה֙ בְּכֶ֣רֶם נָב֔וֹת אֲשֶׁר־יָ֥רַד שָׁ֖ם לְרִשְׁתּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Arise, go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, who [is] in Samaria; behold, in [the] vineyard of Naboth, where he has gone down there to take possession of it.
pieces: "Rise and go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, who reigns in Samaria. He is in Naboth's vineyard right now; he has gone down there to take possession of it.

L.18: "Arise, go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, who [is] in Samaria; look, [he is] in the vineyard of Naboth, where he has gone down to take possession of it.

R.18: "Go down and meet Ahab, the king of Israel, who rules in Samaria. Right now he is in Naboth's vineyard. He has gone there to take it for himself.

decisions.choice: who is in Samaria: whose seat is Samaria
decisions.reason: Ahab is at that moment in the vineyard at Jezreel, so "in Samaria" names the city he rules from, as "king of Samaria" does in verse 1.

decisions.choice: Yahweh's words to Elijah: they run through verse 19
decisions.reason: The quotation opens here and closes at the end of verse 19; the words Elijah is to say to Ahab are quoted inside it.

decisions.choice: reigns (Balanced); rules (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that Samaria is Ahab's capital, not where he is standing (m1).

records.source: וְדִבַּרְתָּ֨ אֵלָ֜יו לֵאמֹ֗ר כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הֲרָצַ֖חְתָּ וְגַם־יָרָ֑שְׁתָּ וְדִבַּרְתָּ֨ אֵלָ֜יו לֵאמֹ֗ר כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה בִּמְק֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֨ר לָקְק֤וּ הַכְּלָבִים֙ אֶת־דַּ֣ם נָב֔וֹת יָלֹ֧קּוּ הַכְּלָבִ֛ים אֶת־דָּמְךָ֖ גַּם־אָֽתָּה׃
records.gloss: And you will speak to him, saying, Thus says Yahweh, Have you murdered and also taken possession? And you will speak to him, saying, Thus says Yahweh, In [the] place where licked the dogs [the] blood of Naboth, will lick the dogs your blood, also you.
pieces: Say to him, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: Have you committed murder and also taken possession?' Then say to him, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: In the place where the dogs licked up Naboth's blood, the dogs will lick up your blood too, yes, yours.'"

L.19: And you will speak to him, saying, 'Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Have you murdered and also taken possession?' And you will speak to him, saying, 'Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: In the place where the dogs licked the blood of Naboth, the dogs will lick your blood, yours too.'"

R.19: Say to him, 'This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: Have you murdered a man and taken his land too?' Then say to him, 'This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: In the same place where dogs licked up Naboth's blood, dogs will lick up your blood too!'"

decisions.choice: have you murdered and also taken possession?: an accusation in the form of a question
decisions.reason: The question needs no answer; it names two crimes. "Murder" is the verb of the commandment "You shall not murder" (Exodus 20:13), and taking a neighbor's field breaks the command not to covet a neighbor's field (Deuteronomy 5:21). Though Jezebel arranged the killing, Yahweh holds Ahab, who profited from it, guilty of it.

decisions.choice: the dogs will lick your blood: fulfilled in part at Ahab's death and fully on his son
decisions.reason: When Ahab died in battle, dogs licked his blood as his chariot was washed at the pool of Samaria (22:38). Because Ahab humbled himself, the full disaster was put off to his son's days (verse 29), and the body of his son Joram was thrown onto Naboth's plot of ground (2 Kings 9:25-26).

decisions.choice: your blood, yours too: emphatic
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats "you" at the end for force: the king will not escape the fate of the man he had killed.

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD (Literal); The LORD says this (Balanced); This is what the LORD says (Readable)
decisions.reason: The prophetic formula is worded as everywhere in Samuel and Kings.

decisions.choice: murdered a man and taken his land
decisions.reason: Readable names the victim and the thing taken, which the Hebrew leaves to the context.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אַחְאָב֙ אֶל־אֵ֣לִיָּ֔הוּ הַֽמְצָאתַ֖נִי אֹיְבִ֑י וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מָצָ֔אתִי יַ֚עַן הִתְמַכֶּרְךָ֔ לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And said Ahab to Elijah, Have you found me, my enemy? And he said, I have found [you], because you sold yourself to do the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh.
pieces: Ahab said to Elijah, "Have you found me, my enemy?" "I have found you," Elijah answered, "because you have sold yourself to do what is evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.20: And Ahab said to Elijah, "Have you found me, my enemy?" And he said, "I have found [you], because you have sold yourself to do the evil in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.20: Ahab said to Elijah, "So, my enemy, have you found me?" Elijah answered, "Yes, I have found you. You have given yourself over to doing what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says is evil.

decisions.choice: found: Ahab means "caught"; Elijah takes up the word
decisions.reason: Ahab feels caught in the act at the vineyard. Elijah answers with the same word: he has found Ahab because of what Ahab has done.

decisions.choice: my enemy: as Ahab once called Elijah "the troubler of Israel"
decisions.reason: Ahab sees the prophet as his personal foe (18:17), not as the bearer of Yahweh's word (compare 22:8).

decisions.choice: you have sold yourself: given yourself over completely, like a slave sold to a master
decisions.reason: The same is said of Ahab in verse 25 and of Israel in 2 Kings 17:17. Ahab is pictured as having handed himself over to evil as its property.

decisions.choice: Elijah's words: they run through verse 24
decisions.reason: Elijah's speech opens here and closes at the end of verse 24. In verses 21-22 Yahweh speaks in the first person through him.

decisions.choice: given yourself over to
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of selling oneself (m3).

decisions.choice: did the evil in the eyes of / what is evil in the sight of / what the LORD says is evil
decisions.reason: The verdict on the kings is worded as everywhere in Kings.

records.source: הִנְנִ֨י מֵבִ֤יא אֵלֶ֨יךָ֙ רָעָ֔ה וּבִעַרְתִּ֖י אַחֲרֶ֑יךָ וְהִכְרַתִּ֤י לְאַחְאָב֙ מַשְׁתִּ֣ין בְּקִ֔יר וְעָצ֥וּר וְעָז֖וּב בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: Behold, I [am] bringing to you evil, and I will burn away after you, and I will cut off to Ahab one urinating against a wall, and shut up and left in Israel.
pieces: I am about to bring disaster on you. I will sweep away those who come after you, and I will cut off from Ahab every male in Israel, bond or free.

L.21: Look, I am bringing disaster on you, and I will sweep away after you, and I will cut off from Ahab [every] one who urinates against a wall, bond and free, in Israel.

R.21: I will bring disaster on you. I will wipe out your family line. I will destroy every man and boy in Ahab's family in Israel, slave or free.

decisions.choice: I: Yahweh speaking through Elijah
decisions.reason: Without a new introduction, Elijah speaks Yahweh's words in the first person, as prophets do. The words are not the ones given in verse 19 but the same judgment that Ahijah spoke against Jeroboam (14:10) and Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha (16:3-4).

decisions.choice: sweep away after you: destroy what is left of you, your line
decisions.reason: The verb is used of burning up or clearing out completely (14:10, "as one burns up dung"; 16:3). "After you" points to those who would come after Ahab, his descendants.

decisions.choice: one who urinates against a wall: a male
decisions.reason: The coarse phrase means every male, from the boy upward, as in 1 Samuel 25:22 and 14:10; 16:11.

decisions.choice: shut up and left: everyone, of every kind
decisions.reason: The pair is not certain. It may mean slave and free, those under restraint and those at liberty, or minors under care and adults. In every reading it means all without exception, as in 14:10 and Deuteronomy 32:36.

decisions.choice: bringing: the form read aloud
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) lack the last letter of this word; the form marked to be read aloud (qere) is the usual spelling of "bringing". The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: every male (Balanced); every man and boy (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the plain sense of the coarse idiom (m3), as in 1 Samuel 25:22; Literal keeps its picture. No gender setting is used, because only males are meant.

decisions.choice: bond and free (Literal); bond or free (Balanced); slave or free (Readable)
decisions.reason: Worded as at 14:10; the decision (m4) keeps the other possible senses.

records.source: וְנָתַתִּ֣י אֶת־בֵּיתְךָ֗ כְּבֵית֙ יָרָבְעָ֣ם בֶּן־נְבָ֔ט וּכְבֵ֖ית בַּעְשָׁ֣א בֶן־אֲחִיָּ֑ה אֶל־הַכַּ֨עַס֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִכְעַ֔סְתָּ וַֽתַּחֲטִ֖א אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And I will make your house like [the] house of Jeroboam son of Nebat and like [the] house of Baasha son of Ahijah, because of the provocation which you provoked, and you caused Israel to sin.
pieces: I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah, because you have provoked {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to anger and have led Israel to sin.

L.22: And I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah, because of the provocation with which you have provoked [{{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}] and [because] you have made Israel sin.

R.22: I will do to your family what I did to the families of Jeroboam son of Nebat and of Baasha son of Ahijah. You have made {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} angry, and you have led Israel into sin.

decisions.choice: the house of Jeroboam, the house of Baasha: two royal families wiped out
decisions.reason: Baasha killed the whole family of Jeroboam (15:29), and Zimri killed the whole family of Baasha (16:11-12), as the prophets had said (14:10-11; 16:3-4). Ahab's line will end the same way.

decisions.choice: your house: your family line, your dynasty
decisions.reason: "House" means the royal family, as with Jeroboam and Baasha.

decisions.choice: provoked: Yahweh is the one provoked
decisions.reason: The verb has no object written, but the formula always means provoking Yahweh to anger (15:30; 16:2, 7, 13).

decisions.choice: me
decisions.reason: The object of "provoked" is supplied (m3), in brackets at Literal.

decisions.choice: I will do to your family what I did to
decisions.reason: Readable states the comparison as an action, which says the same thing in plainer words.

decisions.choice: made Israel sin / led Israel to sin / led Israel into sin; provoked to anger / made angry
decisions.reason: The formulas worded as at 14:9 and 14:16, here said of Ahab.

records.source: וְגַ֨ם־לְאִיזֶ֔בֶל דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר הַכְּלָבִ֛ים יֹאכְל֥וּ אֶת־אִיזֶ֖בֶל בְּחֵ֥ל יִזְרְעֶֽאל׃
records.gloss: And also of Jezebel spoke Yahweh, saying, The dogs will eat Jezebel in [the] rampart of Jezreel.
pieces: And concerning Jezebel {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has also spoken: 'The dogs will eat Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel.'

L.23: And also concerning Jezebel {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken, saying, 'The dogs will eat Jezebel by the rampart of Jezreel.'

R.23: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has also said this about Jezebel: 'Dogs will eat Jezebel by the city wall of Jezreel.'

decisions.choice: rampart: the outer wall or bank of the town
decisions.reason: The word means the outer defenses of a city. Some Hebrew manuscripts and ancient translations read a very similar word, "plot of ground", as in 2 Kings 9:10, 36-37 ("in the plot of ground of Jezreel"). The standard Hebrew text is followed.

decisions.choice: the dogs will eat Jezebel: fulfilled when Jehu came to Jezreel
decisions.reason: Jezebel was thrown from a window at Jezreel, and when men went to bury her, the dogs had left only her skull, feet and hands (2 Kings 9:30-37).

decisions.choice: dogs eating a body: the worst disgrace
decisions.reason: Dogs in ancient towns were scavengers. To lie unburied and be eaten by them was the deepest shame (compare Deuteronomy 28:26).

decisions.choice: wall (Balanced); city wall (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Rampart" is less familiar; Balanced and Readable say "wall".

records.source: הַמֵּ֤ת לְאַחְאָב֙ בָּעִ֔יר יֹאכְל֖וּ הַכְּלָבִ֑ים וְהַמֵּת֙ בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה יֹאכְל֖וּ ע֥וֹף הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: The [one] dying of Ahab in the city, will eat the dogs; and the [one] dying in the field, will eat [the] birds of the heavens.
pieces: Anyone belonging to Ahab who dies in the city, the dogs will eat, and anyone who dies in the open country, the birds of the sky will eat."

L.24: The one belonging to Ahab who dies in the city, the dogs will eat; and the one who dies in the field, the birds of the heavens will eat."

R.24: Dogs will eat anyone in Ahab's family who dies in the city, and birds will eat anyone who dies out in the country."

decisions.choice: the dogs will eat, the birds will eat: the same curse as on Jeroboam and Baasha
decisions.reason: The words are those spoken against the house of Jeroboam (14:11) and the house of Baasha (16:4). None of Ahab's family will receive a proper burial.

decisions.choice: the field: open country outside the town
decisions.reason: "Field" here means the countryside, set against the city: wherever they die, they will not be buried.

decisions.choice: Dogs will eat anyone in Ahab's family
decisions.reason: Readable puts the subject first; Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew order, which puts those who die first. Each level words the sentence as at 14:11 and 16:4.

records.source: רַ֚ק לֹֽא־הָיָ֣ה כְאַחְאָ֔ב אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִתְמַכֵּ֔ר לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה אֲשֶׁר־הֵסַ֥תָּה אֹת֖וֹ אִיזֶ֥בֶל אִשְׁתּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Surely not was like Ahab, who sold himself to do the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh, whom incited him Jezebel his wife.
pieces: There was truly no one like Ahab, who sold himself to do what was evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, urged on by his wife Jezebel.

L.25: Indeed, there was none like Ahab, who sold himself to do the evil in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, whom Jezebel his wife incited.

R.25: There was never anyone like Ahab. He gave himself over to doing what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was evil, and his wife Jezebel urged him on.

decisions.choice: indeed: the narrator's own comment
decisions.reason: Verses 25-26 break into the story to give the writer's verdict on Ahab; the story resumes in verse 27.

decisions.choice: sold himself: gave himself over completely
decisions.reason: As in verse 20.

decisions.choice: incited: stirred up, lured
decisions.reason: The verb is used of enticing someone to wrong, as of one who would lure a family member to serve other gods (Deuteronomy 13:7). Jezebel urged Ahab on, but the verse still holds him responsible.

decisions.choice: gave himself over to
decisions.reason: As in verse 20.

records.source: וַיַּתְעֵ֣ב מְאֹ֔ד לָלֶ֖כֶת אַחֲרֵ֣י הַגִּלֻּלִ֑ים כְּכֹל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשׂ֣וּ הָאֱמֹרִ֔י אֲשֶׁר֙ הוֹרִ֣ישׁ יְהוָ֔ה מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס
records.gloss: And he acted abominably exceedingly, to walk after the idols, according to all that did the Amorite[s] whom dispossessed Yahweh from before [the] sons of Israel.
pieces: He acted in the most detestable way by going after idols, just as the Amorites had done, whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} drove out before the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

L.26: And he acted very abominably in going after the idols, according to all that the Amorites had done, whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} drove out before the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel.

R.26: He did horrible things. He worshiped idols, just as the Amorites had done. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} had forced the Amorites out of the land to make room for the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

decisions.choice: idols: a scornful word for false gods
decisions.reason: The word is used in contempt (Leviticus 26:30; Deuteronomy 29:16). It may be related to a word for dung, though its origin is not certain.

decisions.choice: the Amorites: here, all the peoples of Canaan before Israel
decisions.reason: "Amorites" can stand for all the nations who lived in the land before Israel (Genesis 15:16; 2 Kings 21:11).

decisions.choice: whom Yahweh drove out: Ahab brings back the ways of the nations Yahweh removed
decisions.reason: The nations lost the land because of such practices (Leviticus 18:24-28). By following them, Ahab puts Israel in the same danger.

decisions.choice: going after: following as worshipers
decisions.reason: To "walk after" a god means to serve and worship it (Deuteronomy 6:14).

decisions.choice: worshiped idols
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of "going after" (m4).

decisions.choice: out of the land to make room for
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what "drove out before" Israel meant.

records.source: וַיְהִי֩ כִשְׁמֹ֨עַ אַחְאָ֜ב אֶת־הַדְּבָרִ֤ים הָאֵ֨לֶּה֙ וַיִּקְרַ֣ע בְּגָדָ֔יו וַיָּֽשֶׂם־שַׂ֥ק עַל־בְּשָׂר֖וֹ וַיָּצ֑וֹם וַיִּשְׁכַּ֣ב בַּשָּׂ֔ק וַיְהַלֵּ֖ךְ אַֽט׃ס
records.gloss: And it was, as heard Ahab the words the these, and he tore his clothes and put sackcloth on his flesh and fasted, and he lay in the sackcloth and went about softly.
pieces: When Ahab heard these words, he tore his clothes, put sackcloth on his body, and fasted. He lay down in sackcloth and went about quietly.

L.27: And it happened, when Ahab heard these words, he tore his clothes and put sackcloth on his flesh and fasted, and he lay in the sackcloth and went about softly.

R.27: When Ahab heard this message, he tore his clothes and put on sackcloth, the rough cloth people wore to show grief or sorrow. He did not eat. He even slept in the sackcloth, and he went around quietly and sadly.

decisions.choice: tore his clothes, sackcloth, fasting: signs of grief and repentance
decisions.reason: These were the outward signs of mourning and of turning from sin (Genesis 37:34; 2 Samuel 3:31; Jonah 3:5-8). The fast that Jezebel proclaimed to cover a crime (verse 9) is now kept by Ahab in sorrow.

decisions.choice: softly: slowly, quietly, in a subdued way
decisions.reason: The word means gently or slowly (Isaiah 8:6). It describes a man who goes about humbled and downcast.

decisions.choice: his flesh: his body, next to the skin
decisions.reason: "Flesh" means the body itself: he wore the sackcloth against his skin.

decisions.choice: the rough cloth people wore to show grief or sorrow
decisions.reason: Readable explains sackcloth, as at 2 Samuel 21:10.

records.heading: Ahab humbles himself

records.source: וַֽיְהִי֙ דְּבַר־יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־אֵלִיָּ֥הוּ הַתִּשְׁבִּ֖י לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,
pieces: Then the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Elijah the Tishbite:

L.28: And the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,

R.28: Then this message from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Elijah from Tishbe:

decisions.choice: the word of Yahweh came: the same words as verse 17
decisions.reason: The second message to Elijah is introduced exactly as the first.

decisions.choice: Elijah from Tishbe
decisions.reason: As in verse 17.

records.source: הֲֽרָאִ֔יתָ כִּֽי־נִכְנַ֥ע אַחְאָ֖ב מִלְּפָנָ֑י יַ֜עַן כִּֽי־נִכְנַ֣ע מִפָּנַ֗י לֹֽא־אָבִ֤יא הָֽרָעָה֙ בְּיָמָ֔יו בִּימֵ֣י בְנ֔וֹ אָבִ֥יא הָרָעָ֖ה עַל־בֵּיתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Have you seen that has humbled himself Ahab from before me? Because that he has humbled himself from before me, not I will bring the evil in his days; in [the] days of his son I will bring the evil on his house.
pieces: "Have you noticed how Ahab has humbled himself before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? Since he has humbled himself before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, I will not bring the disaster during his lifetime. I will bring the disaster on his house in his son's days."

L.29: "Have you seen how Ahab has humbled himself before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? Because he has humbled himself before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, I will not bring the disaster in his days; in the days of his son I will bring the disaster on his house."

R.29: "Do you see how Ahab has made himself humble before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? Because he has done this, I will not bring the disaster while he is alive. I will bring it on his family when his son is king."

decisions.choice: Ahab has humbled himself: Yahweh answers even Ahab's repentance
decisions.reason: Yahweh takes note of the humbling of the worst of kings and responds to it, as he later did for Josiah (2 Kings 22:19-20) and for Nineveh (Jonah 3:10). The judgment is put off, not cancelled.

decisions.choice: in the days of his son: fulfilled under Joram
decisions.reason: Ahab's son Joram was killed by Jehu, his body was thrown onto Naboth's plot of ground, and Ahab's seventy sons were killed (2 Kings 9:24-26; 10:1-11).

decisions.choice: I will bring: the form read aloud
decisions.reason: As in verse 21, the written consonants (ketiv) lack the last letter of this verb; the form marked to be read aloud (qere) is the usual spelling. The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: the disaster: the one already announced
decisions.reason: The article points back to the disaster of verse 21.

decisions.choice: when his son is king
decisions.reason: Readable explains "in the days of his son".
